# 2 Samuel Chapter 23 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 196v–197v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_023_page_001.jpg, 2SA_023_page_002.jpg, 2SA_023_page_003.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** Now these are the last words of David:
"The oracle of David the son of Jesse,
the oracle of the man who was raised on high,
the anointed of the God of Jacob,
the sweet singer of Israel:

**2** The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me;
his word was upon my tongue.

**3** The God of Israel has spoken;
the Rock of Israel said to me:
'When one rules justly over men,
ruling in the fear of God,

**4** he is like the light of morning when the sun rises,
a morning without clouds —
from the brightness, from the rain,
grass springs from the earth.'

**5** Is not my house so with God?
For he has made with me an everlasting covenant,
ordered in all things and secure.
Will he not cause all my salvation and all my desire
to flourish?

**6** But the worthless are all like thorns that are thrust away,
for they cannot be taken by hand.

**7** The man who touches them
arms himself with iron and the shaft of a spear,
and they are utterly burned with fire where they lie."

**8** These are the names of David's mighty men: Josheb-basshebeth the Tahchemonite, chief of the Three — he was Adino the Eznite — who killed eight hundred men at one time.

**9** And next to him was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty men. He was with David when they defied the Philistines who were gathered there for battle, and the men of Israel withdrew.

**10** He arose and struck the Philistines until his hand was weary and clung to the sword. And the LORD brought about a great victory that day, and the people returned after him only to strip the slain.

**11** And next to him was Shammah the son of Agee the Hararite. The Philistines gathered at Lehi, where there was a plot of ground full of lentils, and the people fled from the Philistines.

**12** But he took his stand in the middle of the plot, defended it, and struck the Philistines. And the LORD brought about a great victory.

**13** And three of the thirty chief men went down at harvest time and came to David at the cave of Adullam, when a band of Philistines was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.

**14** David was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was then at Bethlehem.

**15** And David said longingly, "Oh, that someone would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem that is beside the gate!"

**16** Then the three mighty men broke through the camp of the Philistines and drew water from the well of Bethlehem that was beside the gate. They carried it and brought it to David, but he would not drink it. He poured it out before the LORD

**17** and said, "Far be it from me, O LORD, that I should do this! Shall I drink the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives?" So he would not drink it. These things the three mighty men did.

**18** Now Abishai, the brother of Joab the son of Zeruiah, was chief of the Thirty. He wielded his spear against three hundred and slew them, and he won a name beside the Three.

**19** He was the most honored of the Thirty and became their commander, but he did not attain to the Three.

**20** And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was a valiant man of Kabzeel, a man of many deeds. He struck down the two sons of Ariel of Moab. He also went down and struck a lion in a pit on a day when snow had fallen.

**21** And he struck down an Egyptian, an impressive man. The Egyptian had a spear in his hand, but Benaiah went down to him with a staff, snatched the spear from the Egyptian's hand, and killed him with his own spear.

**22** These things Benaiah the son of Jehoiada did, and he won a name beside the three mighty men.

**23** He was the most honored of the Thirty but did not attain to the Three. And David set him over his bodyguard.

**24** Asahel the brother of Joab was one of the Thirty:
Elhanan the son of Dodo of Bethlehem,

**25** Shammah the Harodite,
Elika the Harodite,

**26** Helez the Paltite,
Ira the son of Ikkesh of Tekoa,

**27** Abiezer the Anathothite,
Mebunnai the Hushathite,

**28** Zalmon the Ahohite,
Maharai the Netophathite,

**29** Heleb the son of Baanah the Netophathite,
Ittai the son of Ribai of Gibeah of the Benjaminites,

**30** Benaiah the Pirathonite,
Hiddai of the brooks of Gaash,

**31** Abi-albon the Arbathite,
Azmaveth the Barhumite,

**32** Eliahba the Shaalbonite,
the sons of Jashen — Jonathan,

**33** Shammah the Hararite,
Ahiam the son of Sharar the Hararite,

**34** Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai the Maacathite,
Eliam the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,

**35** Hezro the Carmelite,
Paarai the Arbite,

**36** Igal the son of Nathan of Zobah,
Bani the Gadite,

**37** Zelek the Ammonite,
Naharai the Beerothite, the armor-bearer of Joab the son of Zeruiah,

**38** Ira the Ithrite,
Gareb the Ithrite,

**39** Uriah the Hittite — thirty-seven in all.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators agree on the chapter's structure: David's prophetic oracle (vv.1-7), the exploits of the top Three (vv.8-12), the Bethlehem water episode (vv.13-17), the second tier of warriors (vv.18-23), and the full roster of the Thirty (vv.24-39). The textual corruption of v.8 is universally acknowledged. All three recognize the devastating placement of Uriah's name at the end of the list. The poetic section (vv.1-7) presents significant translation challenges due to compressed syntax and agricultural metaphor, but all three translators capture the core imagery of the just ruler as sunrise after rain.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.1 — "utterance/oracle" vs. "declaration"
- **EMET:** "utterance [ne'um]"
- **LOGOS:** "oracle"
- **PNEUMA:** "declaration"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "oracle." The technical prophetic term *ne'um* is best rendered "oracle" (LOGOS), which preserves the claim to prophetic authority.

### V.1 — "the pleasant one of the songs" vs. "the sweet singer" vs. "Israel's beloved songwriter"
- **EMET:** "the-pleasant-one of-[the]-songs [zemirot] of-Yisra'el"
- **LOGOS:** "the sweet singer of Israel"
- **PNEUMA:** "Israel's beloved songwriter"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the sweet singer of Israel." LOGOS preserves the traditional and most recognized rendering. PNEUMA's "songwriter" is anachronistic.

### V.4 — rendering of sunrise/rain metaphor
- **EMET:** "like-[the]-light of-morning, [the]-sun rises, a-morning without clouds; from-brightness, from-rain, grass from-[the]-earth"
- **LOGOS:** "he is like the light of morning when the sun rises, a morning without clouds, when from the brightness after rain the grass springs from the earth"
- **PNEUMA:** "he is like the sunrise on a cloudless morning, like the gleam of sun after rain that makes the grass spring from the earth"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "he is like the light of morning when the sun rises, a morning without clouds — from the brightness, from the rain, grass springs from the earth." Follows LOGOS's structure but retains the Hebrew's compressed parallelism with the dash.

### V.5 — "will he not cause it to sprout" vs. "will he not cause it to flourish"
- **EMET:** "will-he-not cause-[it]-to-sprout [yatsmiyach]?"
- **LOGOS:** "will he not cause it to flourish?"
- **PNEUMA:** "He will surely bring to bloom"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Will he not cause... to flourish?" LOGOS's "flourish" captures *yatsmiyach* (from the root *tsamach*, to sprout/grow) with dignity. PNEUMA's declarative "He will surely" removes the rhetorical question.

### V.10 — "was weary and clung" vs. "cramped and froze"
- **EMET:** "his-hand was-weary [yag'ah], and-clung [tidbaq] his-hand to the-sword"
- **LOGOS:** "his hand was weary and his hand clung to the sword"
- **PNEUMA:** "his hand cramped and froze to his sword"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "his hand was weary and clung to the sword." EMET/LOGOS preserve both Hebrew verbs accurately. PNEUMA's "cramped and froze" is vivid but adds interpretation.

### V.15 — "who will give me to drink" vs. "Oh, that someone would give me" vs. "If only someone would bring me"
- **EMET:** "Who will-give-me-to-drink water"
- **LOGOS:** "Oh, that someone would give me water to drink"
- **PNEUMA:** "If only someone would bring me a drink of water"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Oh, that someone would give me water to drink." LOGOS best renders the Hebrew desiderative *mi yashqeni* with appropriate formality.

### V.16 — "poured it out to YHWH" vs. "poured it out before the LORD" vs. "poured it out on the ground as an offering"
- **EMET:** "he-poured-it-out [vayyassekh] to-YHWH"
- **LOGOS:** "He poured it out before the LORD"
- **PNEUMA:** "he poured it out on the ground as an offering to the LORD"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "He poured it out before the LORD." LOGOS is closest to the Hebrew. PNEUMA adds "on the ground as an offering" — interpretive expansion.

### V.20 — "sons of Ariel of Moab" vs. "champion fighters of Moab"
- **EMET:** "the-two [sons of]-Ari'el of-Moav"
- **LOGOS:** "the two sons of Ariel of Moab"
- **PNEUMA:** "two champion fighters of Moab"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the two sons of Ariel of Moab." The Hebrew reads *ariel* (lion of God), likely a proper name or title. PNEUMA's "champion fighters" is too interpretive.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
